{{nihongo|'''Hikawami Shrine'''|御井神社 (斐川町)}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Hikawa-chō Naoe, {{ill|Izumo, Shimane|Q825166|qid=Q825166}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}. It is a shrine associated with traditions concerning Yagami-hime, who appears in the {{ill|Myth of Ōkuninushi|Q11433656|qid=Q11433656}}, and her child {{ill|Kimata-no-Kami|Q11092833|qid=Q11092833}} (this deity), and is worshipped as a god of safe childbirth. {{nihongo|'''Hikawami Shrine'''|御井神社 (斐川町)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumo Province]].

== Enshrined deity ==
* Konamata-no-Kami (Mii-no-Kami)

He appears in the myths of {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōanamuchi-no-Kami}} depicted in the '{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}'. Yagami-hime, who married Ōkuninushi, became pregnant and came as far as {{ill|Izumo Province|Q582846|qid=Q582846}}, but fearing the principal wife {{ill|Suseri-Hime|Q8191715|qid=Q8191715|lt=Suseri-bime}}, she pushed the newborn child into the fork of a tree and returned to {{ill|Inaba Province|Q1054338|qid=Q1054338}}. Because of this, the child was named Konamata-no-Kami.

== History ==
The shrine is identified with the Mii Shrine listed as an existing government shrine (zaishingi-kan-sha) in the Izumo District entry of the '{{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|qid=Q11395858}}', and with the Mii Shrine recorded in the Izumo District of Izumo Province in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'. Near the shrine grounds, the Sugisawa III site—where nine post holes believed to be the remains of an ancient {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|Q387874|qid=Q387874}} shrine building were excavated—has been discovered, and is presumed to have been the original shrine site.

== Subsidiary and branch shrines ==
* Tenjin Shrine
* Jisson Shrine (じっそんじんじゃ) – an off-site shrine that enshrines the mother deity Yagami-hime

== Faith ==
Near the shrine are three {{ill|Well|Q43483|qid=Q43483}} called “Ikui,” “Sakui,” and “Tsunagai,” and there is a tradition that Yagami-hime used their water for the birth bath at the time of childbirth. It is thought that worship of these three wells originally developed into the shrine.
